title: SLO-aligned regional throttle orchestration with graded circuit breakers and fairness-preserving shedder
creator: Anika Sharma
description:
Problem: We observed cascading latency spikes and tenant unfairness during cross-region failovers and transient limiter outages. Current limiter behavior is binary (open/closed) per region which causes either full passthrough (risking SLO breach) or blunt shedding that disproportionately impacts small/high-priority tenants. Goal: implement an orchestration layer that maps SLO budgets to regional admission decisions, applies graded circuit-breakers (latency-first -> token-fraction -> full-cutover), and preserves soft fairness across tenants during degraded operation.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: per-tenant SLO budgets (token and latency windows), regional circuit-breaker state machine, fractional token allocation (token-fractioner), lease-based handoff for limits during failover, telemetry and dashboards, canary rollout path.
- Out of scope: full rewrite of the runtime admission logic; deep model-architecture-specific kernel changes (handled by runtime team).

Design summary:
1) SLO budget controller: maintain rolling SLO budgets per tenant and per-region (tokens, p95 latency headroom). Budgets are fed by Console SLO configs and runtime telemetry.
2) Graded breaker states: GREEN (normal), YELLOW (constrain batch concurrency + prefer small requests), ORANGE (token-fraction: allocate a % of normal tokens per window), RED (aggressive shedding + route to fallback model variants). Each state has region and global triggers (e.g., sustained p95 > 2x target for 30s, token consumption > 110% of reserved capacity).
3) Fairness layer: proportional allocation using sticky windows and decay: proportional_share = min(1, tenant_budget / sum_active_budgets) with a fairness_index metric to detect starvation and apply credit rebalancing over a 10-minute window.
4) Lease handoff & multi-region failover: when a region degrades, active leases (short-lived soft leases for burst capacity) can be drained and transferred to neighboring regions with capacity; transfer uses a two-phase commit with time-bounded grace to avoid double-spend of token budgets.
5) Telemetry & ops: new metrics (shed_rate, fractional_alloc_pct, fairness_index, region_lease_drain_seconds, slo_budget_utilization) and a playbackable simulation dashboard.

Implementation plan:
- Stage 1 (design + simulation): prototype token-fractioner and breaker state machine in sim harness; produce deterministic scenarios (burst, regional blackhole, noisy neighbor) and tune thresholds.
- Stage 2 (runtime canary): implement admission hooks and state machine behind feature flag; deploy to staging then canary region (eu-west-1) with limited tenants.
- Stage 3 (observability + playbooks): build dashboards, automated alerts, runbook for ops.
- Stage 4 (graduated rollout): expand across regions and enable for P1/P2 tenants, monitor for fairness regressions.

Risk & trade-offs:
- Complexity: introducing fractional allocations and lease handoffs increases admission logic complexity; mitigated by strict feature flags, unit tests and a sim harness.
- Latency vs throughput: fractional allocations may increase tail latency for some workloads; breaker tuning will bias towards preserving p95 SLOs at cost of throughput.
- Consistency: two-phase lease handoffs risk transient over-allocation; time-bounded leases and idempotent token accounting will limit window of double-allocation.

acceptance_criteria: Simulations show >50% reduction in SLO breach minutes during regional blackholes compared to current limiter
No tenant experiences >30% sustained reduction in allocated tokens without elevated priority label during canary
Dashboards emit the new metrics and alerts (p95 headroom < configured threshold) during canary
Canary rollout documented with rollback trigger thresholds and automated feature-flag kill switch

rollback_plan: Feature-flagged deployment with automated kill switch. Rollback triggers: sustained p95 > 2x target for 10m, fairness_index < 0.6 for >5% tenants for 5m, or any double-allocation detected. Rollback steps: disable FF, revert PR, trigger lease drain reverse, notify affected tenants via incident channel.
next_steps: Finish infra review on PR, run staging canary (eu-west-1) for 48h with 20 tenants, finalize Console UI labels and opt-in flow, schedule chaos test (region partition + limiter outage) on 2026-03-18.
owner_notes: Prioritize robust telemetry and clear rollbacks over aggressive optimization. The sim harness must be able to replay production traces for validation before wider rollout.
